definitions.explanation: The number 10,000,000, written with the explicit {一|いち} (one) prefix on {千万|せんまん} (ten million) for clarity, most often in formal documents, contracts, and on checks or invoices where the amount must be unambiguous.

examples.japanese: {一千万|いっせんまん}⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧⟦{借|か}りた→借りる：00532_kariru⟧。
⟦{契約書|けいやくしょ}→契約書：06416_keiyakusho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{金額|きんがく}→金額：02665_kingaku⟧{一千万|いっせんまん}⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{記|しる}された。
examples.english: The contract stated the amount as ten million yen.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小切手|こぎって}→小切手：06305_kogitte⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、あとで⟦{数字|すうじ}→数字：03361_suuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}き{加|くわ}えられない→書き加える：22619_kakikuwaeru⟧よう「{一千万|いっせんまん}⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{漢数字|かんすうじ}→漢数字：28128_kansuuji⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: On a check, you write "ten million yen" in kanji numerals so that no digits can be added later.

notes:
{一千万|いっせんまん} (ten million) is the same value as ⟦{千万|せんまん}→千万：28267_senman⟧, but with the ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧ (one) written explicitly. Ordinary speech usually drops it and just says ⟦{千万|せんまん}→千万：28267_senman⟧えん, but ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧ is added in formal writing to prevent the number from being altered or misread.

USAGE:
Seen especially on legal documents, contracts, receipts, and bank forms, where {一千万|いっせんまん} makes clear that no digit precedes ⟦{千万|せんまん}→千万：28267_senman⟧. Formal kanji numerals ({壱千万|いっせんまん}, using {壱|いち} instead of ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧) are used on checks and official documents for the same anti-fraud reason.
